title: The audience boundary cases decide exactly as the table says, in both the pure function and the SQL predicate
mechanism: one shared case table compiled into both test binaries

cd backend && CONCERT_TEST_DATABASE_URL=... cargo +1.88.0 test --locked -p concert-service --test intro_visibility_contract
commands.note: 8 passed against a real PostgreSQL 16 cluster; every_shared_case_agrees_between_the_pure_function_and_sql covers the whole table

cases.what: no age bound and gender any is visible to a viewer with no claim, and the claim port is never called
the minimum age is inclusive: a viewer exactly at the minimum is admitted
the maximum age is exclusive: a viewer exactly at maximum_age_exclusive is denied
an expired post is denied to a non-author even when the audience would admit them
a draft is denied to a non-author
the author sees their own post whatever its state and audience
a block in either direction denies even an unrestricted post
the current age is derived with the Seoul-date rule, so a birthday boundary agrees between the pure function and SQL

limitations: The page and detail scopes carry one block state per request, so a viewer who has blocked anyone is reported as blocking everyone. That over-denies and never over-admits; a per-row block join is the correct long-term shape.

The page query evaluates the author's account standing through concert_world_account_deletion_fences; the detail query uses the scope's author_standing. Both are concert-local and neither joins across services.
